title: Validating Drug Efficacy and Safety in 96-Well Platforms of Human Cortical Organoids
author: Krieg, Rachad, et al.
materials: STEMdiff Dorsal Forebrain Organoid Differentiation Kit

steps.title: Thaw and seed A375 melanoma cells
steps.instruction: Warm A375 Complete Medium to room temperature (20‑25 °C). Thaw a cryovial of A375 single‑cell suspension in a 37 °C water bath for 1–2 min, transfer to a Falcon tube and add 9 mL pre‑warmed DMEM/F12. Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL A375 Complete Medium and seed 1 × 10⁶ cells into a T75 flask containing 12 mL A375 Complete Medium. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C.

steps.title: Maintain and passage melanoma cultures
steps.instruction: Change medium the next day and thereafter every other day. Passage cells every 3–4 days when 70–90 % confluent: wash each T75 flask with D‑PBS, add 5 mL Trypsin‑EDTA and incubate 3–5 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C); detach cells by gentle pipetting, transfer to a Falcon tube, add 10 mL DMEM/F12, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL A375 Complete Medium and seed at a 1:10–1:20 ratio into new T75 flasks containing 12 mL A375 Complete Medium. Allow cells to settle 24 h at 37 °C. Keep one T75 flask ready for organoid day 43; therefore thaw A375 cells no later than organoid day 35‑37 and passage at least once before use.

steps.title: Design 96‑well plate layout
steps.instruction: Create a layout that avoids border wells and includes at least three technical replicates per compound‑concentration condition. For single‑concentration screens assign a negative control (solvent, e.g., 0.1 % DMSO) and a positive control (encorafenib + binimetinib at 10 µM). For 10‑point concentration‑response curves select a range covering reported IC₅₀ or clinically relevant doses, start with the highest concentration, and place the negative control in the last column.

steps.title: Prepare compound stocks and assay plates
steps.instruction: Make fresh 10 mM compound stocks in DMSO, aliquot into low‑binding polypropylene plates, seal, and store at –20 °C. Before use, remove plates, equilibrate to room temperature (20‑25 °C), and centrifuge to prevent spill‑over and avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles. For concentration‑response assays prepare a 2‑step serial dilution in DMSO aiming for a final DMSO concentration of 0.1 % in the assay medium. Transfer diluted compounds to assay‑ready 96‑well plates according to the designed layout. Automated liquid handlers (e.g., ECHO) may be used, or the procedure can be performed manually.

steps.title: Live imaging of organoid plates
steps.instruction: Place plates (with lid) into the EnSight multimode plate reader (or equivalent) and image at 37 °C, or limit exposure to ≤20 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C). Acquire brightfield and the appropriate fluorescence channel (RFP or GFP) using seven Z‑planes spanning ~1800 µm. Imaging settings: Brightfield – excitation 735 nm, power 4 %, exposure 4 ms; RFP – excitation 525 nm, power 100 %, exposure 30 ms; GFP – excitation 465 nm, power 4 %, exposure 4 ms. Optional: perform Z‑stack processing for representative images.

steps.title: Batch image processing and analysis
steps.instruction: Using Kaleido software, segment each organoid as the largest round object in the brightfield channel, then analyze organoid morphology (size, roundness) and quantify fluorescence intensity within the segmented region. Apply the following detection parameters: brightness limit 0.6, flat‑field correction scale 0, minimum object size 100 000 µm², minimum contrast ‘very relaxed’, ring‑shaped objects = yes, largest objective only = yes. Well detection settings: channel = automatic, exclude well margin 400 px, mode = small well, well dimensions = automatic, well shape = round, well diameter = 6.3 mm. Exclude free‑floating cancer cells from analysis.

steps.title: Normalize data and generate dose‑response curves
steps.instruction: Calculate the average autofluorescence of untreated hCOs in medium and subtract this value from all MBM fluorescence readings. Set the average fluorescence (or luminescence) of negative‑control wells (0.1 % DMSO) as 100 % viability. Compute relative viability for each compound‑treated well as (Intensity sample / Intensity mean negative control) × 100 %. Plot normalized viability versus compound concentration in GraphPad Prism (or similar), fit a four‑parameter variable‑slope sigmoidal model, and extract IC₅₀ and maximal efficacy (Emax) values.

steps.title: Quality‑control calculations (SNR & CV)
steps.instruction: Calculate signal‑to‑noise ratio (SNR) as (mean MBM signal – mean hCO autofluorescence) / standard deviation of hCO autofluorescence. Determine coefficient of variation (CV) by (standard deviation of replicates / mean of replicates) × 100 % in GraphPad Prism.
